newsitem.title: UK: UK's Major sees sharp divide with Labour over EU.
newsitem.headline: UK's Major sees sharp divide with Labour over EU.

text.p: British Prime Minister John Major said on Tuesday there was now a clear divide between his Conservative Party and opposition Labour over Europe. "There is now clearly exposed a sharp dividing line between the parties on Europe," Major told a news conference.

Major said he opposed the transfer of further powers to Brussels with the employment chapter, the extension of qualified majority voting and new powers for the European parliament. He said Labour leader Tony Blair says yes to all of those.
Major said he also rejected European control of foreign policy. "Mr Blair says maybe, that means yes."
The idea of having foreign policy decided by majority voting was "absurd", Major said. Earlier, Blair had said he would not cede control of defence, taxation and immigration to the European Union.

Major said European Commission president Jacques Santer had made it clear on Monday that other countries in Europe wished to secure further European integration. "And Mr Blair made a speech in which he made it clear that many of these objectives are objectives Labour share," Major said.
On Monday, Santer attacked what he called Eurosceptic "doom merchants." Both Labour and Conservative leaders criticised his intervention.

"It's only a Conservative government that can be trusted to say no to a federal Europe, no to the Social Chapter, no to new employment laws and no to entry into a single currency without a referendum of all the people," Major said.

Both Labour and the Conservatives officially keep the option open of joining a single currency in 1999. Labour supports an EU directive on maximum working hours and the Social Chapter which guarantees minimum employment rights. The Conservatives do not.
Elections are due in nine days with Labour well ahead in the polls.
